news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire reports 67 vacant surplus former operational assets against a portfolio of 549
news_drafts.lead:
Aberdeenshire Council had 67 vacant surplus former operational assets at the first quarter of 2026/27, according to the Business Services performance report for the Business Services Committee. Its operational portfolio, the buildings and sites it still uses, stands at 549 at the second quarter.

The paper says the number of vacant assets is expected to fall in 2026/27 and 2027/28. A number of closures are planned for early 2027, linked to a new depot and office facility at One Harlaw Road, Inverurie. The performance target for capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is 100% of the amount budgeted.

The committee also has the Business Services budget risk register for 2026/27. It identifies a pressure on income from licensing fees and charges. In the register's words, "Pressure has been identified within Licensing fees and charges however this is currently being offset with underspends across the wider Business Services budget." The risk score for council tax and fees-and-charges collection remains at 16, unchanged, with a residual score of 12.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

findings.paper_title: Scrutiny Referral from Audit Committee Meeting 10 September 2026 (Internal Audit Report 2710 - ECS Procurement)
findings.headline: The audit action deadlines are 31 March 2027, while the report gives 4 February 2027 and 18 March 2027 as dates for the Stage 1 Report.
findings.detail: The management response sets 31 March 2027 as the deadline for the ECS, CPSS and Learning and Organisational Development audit actions. The recommendations ask for a Stage 1 Report on 4 February 2027, but the options section gives 18 March 2027 as the date to be agreed with Committee Services. The report is due to be reported verbally to the Audit Committee on 10 December 2026.
findings.matters: The gap between the audit action deadline and the Stage 1 Report date, and the two different Stage 1 dates in the paper, show how a council schedules a remediation review against its own audit deadlines.
findings.quote: The audit action deadlines are 31 March 2027 for the ECS, CPSS and Learning and Organisational Development tasks.

findings.paper_title: Scrutiny Referral from Audit Committee Meeting 10 September 2026 (Internal Audit Report 2710 - ECS Procurement)
findings.headline: The audit identified three Major-rated findings on governance and oversight, procurement planning and approval, and procurement routes and Best Value.
findings.detail: Two further findings, on procurement transparency and record keeping and on contract management, were rated Moderate. The report sets out these five findings as the basis for the Committee Review Process.
findings.matters: Three Major findings covering approvals and Best Value give other finance officers a specific checklist of the procurement controls an internal audit can test and rate as Major.
findings.figures: three Major-rated findings; two Moderate-rated findings
findings.quote: The audit identified three Major-rated findings: governance and oversight; procurement planning and approval arrangements; and procurement routes and Best Value.

findings.paper_title: Scrutiny Referral from Audit Committee Meeting 10 September 2026 (Internal Audit Report 2710 - ECS Procurement)
findings.headline: ECS procurement records approximately 150,000 purchases through 32,458 invoices, with a total value of £122.5m in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The management response gives this as the scale of ECS procurement activity. The audit reviewed a sample of 25 purchases. ECS says this scale supports a proportionate, risk-based improvement programme but does not diminish the significance of the weaknesses identified.
findings.matters: The size of the spend under review, with a value of £122.5m for one directorate in a single year, is the exposure a finance director would use to judge how far a procurement control gap could reach.
findings.figures: approximately 150,000 purchases; 32,458 invoices; £122.5m in 2025/26; sample of 25 purchases
findings.quote: with a total value of £122.5m in 2025/26

findings.paper_title: Scrutiny Referral from Audit Committee Meeting 10 September 2026 (Internal Audit Report 2710 - ECS Procurement)
findings.headline: The Audit Committee voted 7 to 6 that it was not assured by the ECS procurement audit and referred the matter to the Education and Children's Services Committee.
findings.detail: Following discussion, the Audit Committee agreed it was not assured and referred the matter to the Education and Children's Services Committee to commence Stage 1 of the Committee Review Process. The referral covers all points raised within the audit.
findings.matters: A split committee vote sending an audit to a policy committee for a formal review shows a governance escalation route that other councils' audit committees may face on similar findings.
findings.quote: the Committee agreed that it was not assured and referred the matter

findings.paper_title: Scrutiny Referral from Audit Committee Meeting 10 September 2026 (Internal Audit Report 2710 - ECS Procurement)
findings.headline: Internal Audit Report 2710 assessed net risk as Major at Directorate level and provided Limited assurance over ECS goods and services procurement.
findings.detail: The report states that the audit assessed net risk as Major at Directorate level and gave Limited assurance. ECS accepts the audit findings and its responsibility for strengthening procurement governance, compliance and assurance.
findings.matters: A Major net risk rating and Limited assurance from internal audit on a service's procurement is the kind of control finding that a finance director, here or at another council, would want to compare against their own procurement controls.
findings.figures: Major net risk at Directorate level; Limited assurance
findings.quote: provided Limited assurance over ECS goods and services procurement
